decision: Implementation of WF-134 meets the release bar

state.change_summary: WF-134 adds a deal-health workflow as a plugin: one new domain module in the shared competitive_baseline package (backend/dsr/competitive_baseline/deal_health.py), one feature module with 23 routes on /api/wf-134 (backend/dsr/features/wf134_engagement_driven_deal_health_scoring_risk_detection_and_coaching.py), two backend test files (backend/tests/test_wf134.py, backend/tests/test_wf134_http.py) and one frontend feature folder (frontend/src/features/wf-134-deal-health/). The workflow scores a deal from engagement decay, unreviewed key material and stakeholder coverage, raises a risk alert and one coaching cue per active reason when the score drops, and closes the loop with a readiness reading built from recorded coaching outcomes. It owns its own engagement intake, imports the store and nothing else from dsr in the domain module, adds no shared-file edit, no migration and no typed column, and every write routes through AuditedDatabase with an audit source derived from the router.

declared_unverified: A mid-build jev.py decide: the bridge answers jev.py doctor and the pinned release-bar, but returns HTTP 502 for a payload whose questions are all choice, on four attempts including a two-question variant and a single-choice ask. The design decisions are recorded in the served vocabulary instead.
Browser validation of the merged feature: that is the pass owner's step after the merge, and this branch renders no screenshot.
Contrast ratios, responsive breakpoints at 375/768/1024/1440, and keyboard reachability: the mechanical design-floor check does not measure them.
The vendor numbers the research quotes: one vendor makes written guarantees about quota attainment and forecast accuracy, and this product has no evidence for either, so neither is stated anywhere.

Two earlier local runs of the whole backend suite failed on tests/test_seed.py, which runs backend/seed.py as a subprocess against a 300s timeout. It is a local-host effect, not this change: this feature's own seed costs 0.056s, the same two tests time out with this feature's module renamed away, and both passed in CI.
state.requirements: A feature adds files and edits no shared file. All reads and writes go through dsr.deps / RecordStore / AuditedDatabase so every mutation writes its audit row in the same transaction. Payloads stay schema-flexible JSON: no migration, no typed column, the envelope untouched. The feature owns a unique route prefix with no colliding concrete (method, path) pair. Tests exist and the whole suite is green. The frontend page builds, is discovered by the glob, and meets the design floor.

criteria.true: Every surface the change introduces is exercised by a measurement, with at most incidental limits declared

criteria.true: Writes go through the audited store and the envelope is unchanged
criteria.false: A direct connection is opened, or a typed column or migration is added

design_floor.instructions: Does the frontend meet the design floor -- 44px touch targets, visible focus, a text label beside every icon, no emoji as icons, reduced motion respected -- as checked by the scripted pass?

criteria.true: The scripted design-floor pass is green
criteria.false: The pass is red, was skipped, or is on the allowlist

verdict.instructions: Should this change land on main? Weigh the balance of the questions above rather than deciding on your own: where contract_compliance, audit_integrity and design_floor are all healthy and the evidence questions show broad coverage, answer merge with the confidence that warrants. Items listed as unverified are declared context to weigh, not defects in themselves -- but a change whose coverage is genuinely thin, or which was recovered from a base far behind main and not reconciled, is fix.

criteria.merge: Evidence supports landing it: suite green, contract intact, floor met
criteria.fix: Worth keeping but needs work against current main before landing
